doc: Generated by scripts/schema/generate.mjs from schema/cloudkit-schema.json. Do not edit: change the JSON and run `node scripts/schema/generate.mjs` (docs/cloudkit-schema-design.md §12.1). The Setting record keys (§3.5.3): one record per key, account scope in Library and space scope in a space. Generated into schema/generated/settings-catalog.json, which the hosted MCP and the web validate Setting writes against; ForeverLMMacUnitTests/SettingsCatalogTests fails when it and the app disagree (SyncedPreferenceKeys, set_app_setting's catalog, AITaskSettingsCatalog). keys and families list every synced key and prefix that stays a Setting; records lists the ones generation 2 moves into typed records (the domain prefixes of §10, which are not Settings), origin spec marking one the spec maps before every generation-1 build writes it; leftOut lists the synced prefixes that stay Settings but stay out of the catalog, because only their own writers set them, never set_app_setting. type is SettingValue.t; mcp names how a chat sets the key (derived: the setter computes it); retired keys are kept for older builds and never written; origin spec marks a key the spec defines that no client writes yet. A family pattern is literal text with <name> placeholders; a placeholder matches one or more characters, and parts restricts it to a list (aiTasks: aiTasks.ids). An exact key never starts with a family's, a record's or a left-out prefix, and no prefix is listed twice.

aiRoute.task..doc: A Background task's model of its own, which wins over Background's (KeychainService.ownRoute, Settings › Background › Tasks): the AIModelRoutePreference JSON {version, provider, model}. readAloud.voiceRating..doc: The learner's thumbs on one model's voice (ArticleSpeechVoiceRating); absent is no rating.

notebook.thinkFirst..doc: One notebook's Think first level, the learner's own (account scope, so a teammate's choice never changes it), over thinkFirst.level; absent means the library's level applies. A Setting rather than a NotebookState field, like notebook.naming., so no store schema changes.

follow..doc: A space's explicit refresh of a followed Collection: {autoImport, runnerDeviceID}, naming the one member's Mac that imports the feed (§3.5.5). The Mac writes it through SpaceFollows, not as a synced preference: the catalog's origin spec only says no preference key carries it.

map.layout..doc: One of the learner's canvases (docs/knowledge-map-design.md, "Canvases in the Space"), as a JSON string {version, placements, regions, edges, removed, name, created, trash} (KnowledgeMapLayout): each placed card's spot, each region the learner drew and each arrow, every entry stamped with the time it was written and every removal kept as a tombstone, so two copies merge entry by entry; and the canvas itself, its name and Trash mark stamped the same way and the second it was made. One row per canvas, and every row is a canvas listed in the Space: mapID is library for the first canvas, else cnv- and a lowercase UUID. Written by the Canvas pane, the Space and MCP's canvas tools on the Mac, never set_app_setting: a lens a chat asks for changes nothing until the learner keeps it.

aiSeeded.task..doc: That ForeverLM gave the task its starting model of its own, once for the account (true); absent until then. Written only by KeychainService.seedCanvasVoiceRoute, seedCardAnswerCheckRoute and seedGoDeeperRoute, so a learner who sends Canvas Voice, Card Answer Check or Go Deeper back to Background's model is not given the starting model again, on this Mac or another; never set_app_setting.

notebook.naming..doc: The name and card description ForeverLM last put on a notebook made without a name, as a JSON string {title, summary?, sources?, exchanges?} (NotebookNaming.Mark): ForeverLM may rename the notebook only while its title and summary are still these. Absent means ForeverLM leaves the name alone; every learner edit of the title or description removes it. Written by the notebook creators and the naming step (Mac, iPhone, MCP create_project without a title), never set_app_setting.

studio.workspaceView..doc: One saved workspace view per row (StudioSavedWorkspaceView), so monitor arrangements never contend: the window arrangement the learner saved with Save Workspace View, as the window's own stored form. Written by the window that saves or deletes it, never set_app_setting: a chat has no window to arrange.

notebook.questions..doc: The questions a notebook's guide suggested for its sources, and which were asked, as a JSON string {sources, questions, asked} (NotebookSuggestedQuestions.Kept): sources is the fingerprint of the notebook's source ids the questions were suggested for; the guide offers the questions not asked yet in every new chat without a model call, and offers Suggest questions again only when the fingerprint changes. Per member, one row per notebook. Written by the Mac's notebook chat when an answer suggests questions or one is asked, never set_app_setting.

notebookCollection..doc: A Notebook Collection's name (a leading emoji is its icon), one Setting per collection, null once the collection is deleted. Written by the collection writers (the Notebooks home on each client, MCP update_notebook_collection on the Mac), never set_app_setting (§3.5.3).

pageSpace..doc: The name of one of the learner's spaces of pages (PageSpaces; ChatGPT's spaces, the Space sidebar's Spaces), a leading emoji its icon; spaceID is psp- and a lowercase UUID. One Setting per space, null once the space is deleted. The learner's own grouping, not a sync space (D4): written by the Space sidebar on the Mac and the web and by MCP update_space on the Mac, never set_app_setting.

pageSpaceTrash..doc: When one of the learner's spaces of pages (pageSpace.<spaceID>) went to Trash, as whole seconds since 1970 in text; absent while the space is in use (PageSpaces; Codex's Space Trash holds spaces as well as pages). A space in Trash leaves the sidebar and lists no pages, its pages stay in All and keep their page.space rows, so Restore brings the space back as it was; Delete Forever removes the name, the page rows and this row. A row whose pageSpace name is gone is read past. Written by the Space on the Mac and the web, never set_app_setting.

page.space..doc: The one space of pages (pageSpace.<spaceID>) a page, linked Google Doc, site or reading is in, as its spaceID; absent when it is in none. One Setting per record, per member, never a field of the Doc: an id whose pageSpace name is gone (deleted, or not arrived yet) is read past, and deleting a space removes the rows naming it that the deleting device holds. Written by Move to Space and New page in a space on the Mac and the web, and by MCP update_space on the Mac, never set_app_setting.

page.pinned..doc: When the learner pinned a page, a linked Google Doc or a site (PagePins; ChatGPT's Pin, the Space sidebar's Pinned section), as the whole seconds since 1970 in text; absent when it is not pinned, and the newest pin lists first. One Setting per record, per member, never a field of the Doc: only the learner's own pages pin, never a team's. Written by Pin and Unpin on the Mac and the web, never set_app_setting.

chat.pinned..doc: When the learner pinned a chat, or the place a drag gave it (ChatPins; Codex's Pin chat, Home's Pinned section), as whole seconds since 1970 in text; absent when it is not pinned, and the highest lists first. One Setting per chat, per member, never a field of the Chat; a day's memory review never pins. Written by Pin Chat, Unpin Chat and a drag in Pinned on the Mac and the web, and by MCP update_review_session is_pinned on the Mac, never set_app_setting.

page.parent..doc: The page a page is nested under (PageParents; ChatGPT's subpages, the Space lists' nested rows), as the parent's Artifact id; absent when the page is top-level. One Setting per child, per member, never a field of the Doc: only the learner's own Markdown pages nest, under another of their own, never a team's. An id that names a page that is gone, in Trash or not the learner's own is read past (its children list at the top and the row stays, so restoring the parent brings them back), and a cycle two devices made at once is cut at its smallest id. Written by Move to Page, New Subpage, Remove from Parent and the editor's Page row on the Mac, never set_app_setting.

spaceList..doc: One of the learner's lists in the Space (SpaceLists; ChatGPT's To-do list among the pages): a list of goals or of ideas, as a JSON string {kind: goals|ideas, name, created, at, trashed} in seconds since 1970, trashed absent while it is in use; listID is lst- and a lowercase UUID. One Setting per list, the newer write winning whole, null once deleted forever. The learner's own grouping: the goals and ideas stay records of their own. Written by the Space on the Mac and by MCP's list tools there, never set_app_setting.

spaceListItem..doc: The one list in the Space (spaceList.<listID>) a goal or an idea is in, as its listID; absent when it is in none. One Setting per record, per member, never a field of the goal or idea: an id whose list row is gone is read past, and deleting a list removes the rows naming it that the deleting device holds. Written by the Space on the Mac and by MCP's list tools there, never set_app_setting.

reader.pdfRotations..doc: The pages of one PDF source the learner turned in the reader, as a JSON string {"<page>": <degrees>}: a zero-based page of the source (a chapter of a book counts from its own first page; a page before the first chapter is negative), clockwise degrees in 90, 180 or 270 added to the page's own rotation in the file, a page turned full circle left out. One Setting per source, per member, never a field of the Source: the library file is shared and never rewritten for a reading preference, and a team's copy of the source carries no member's turns. Written by Rotate Page in the Mac reader, never set_app_setting; the iPhone and the web do not read it yet.

images.notebookCoverBackfill..doc: The cover backfill's claim and completion marker for one zone (D53, §5.9): {state: running|done, by: deviceID, at}, in Library, a space's in its owner's Library. No synced preference: only the backfill on the maintenance Mac writes it, by a compare-and-set save beside the engine, never through user_preferences; set_app_setting on the Mac and in the hosted MCP refuses it, and the web and the iPhone never write it.
